title: Quarter Scout: Brief and Exec Spotlight — Q2 planning (working)
content:
Purpose: a compact working brief for the leadership cohort and ops partners to land a minimal, high-confidence set of company priorities for the next quarter. This doc is intentionally short — focus is alignment + executable asks for exec update and the company town spotlight.

Context and constraints:
- Heads-down signals from Q1: Dedicated sales motions accelerating; hosted API latency targets largely met but cost per token trending up in high-concurrency workloads; Private deployment RFPs increasing demand for compliance artifacts.
- Resourcing: hiring plateau on infra/serving (two IC offers outstanding). Need to pick 3 cross-company priorities we can staff and measure.
- Goal for the weekend sync: finalize OKR seed, decide townline narrative, identify 6-week rapid experiments.

Top-level ask to execs (one paragraph):
We need a clear, defendable short-list of priorities that trade depth for speed: 1) stabilize unit economics on hosted inference for high-concurrency customers, 2) close Dedicated capacity SLA gaps for top 10 customers, 3) convert 2 high-propensity compliance leads into Private pilots. Each priority should have a named owner, an explicit success metric, and a 6-week experiment plan.

Draft OKRs (seed — plz edit):
- Objective 1: Reduce per-token cost for high-concurrency text generation by 20% while holding p95 latency within SLA.
  - KR1: Achieve 20% lower GPU-hours/token on 3 benchmark workloads (lobby, search, chat) (owner: Priya Shah).
  - KR2: Deploy intelligent batching & KV caching defaults to 80% of high-concurrency traffic (owner: Platform SWAT).
  - KR3: Post-rollout, maintain p95 request latency <= SLA for 95% of requests (owner: SRE).

- Objective 2: Harden Dedicated offering to reach a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA and improve provisioning time.
  - KR1: Reduce mean time to provision Dedicated pool from 6 hours to 30 minutes for standard configs (owner: Jordan Kim).
  - KR2: Implement canary fallback policy across zones and measure failover recovery time < 5 minutes (owner: Infra).
  - KR3: Close top 5 reliability bugs contributing to incidents in Q1 (owner: Serving runtime).

- Objective 3: Expand Private deployment pipeline for regulated customers.
  - KR1: Convert 2 enterprise prospects to Private pilot contracts (owner: GTM-Enterprise).
  - KR2: Publish an audited compliance checklist & deployment runbook for customers (owner: Security & Compliance).
  - KR3: Deliver KMS/HSM integration reference for on-prem installs (owner: Private Deployments PM).

Exec update highlights (to be read by CEO in 6 min slot):
- Q1 wins: shipped streaming + function calling on hosted API, onboarded 3 mid-market Dedicated customers, closed 1 Private pilot LOI.
- Metrics snapshot (quick bullets): MRR +12% q/q, Hosted token spend +18% driven by 2 large customers, avg p95 latency within SLA but visible tail on high-concurrency.
- Ask of execs: approve the three priorities above, commit to single-threaded owners for each, and authorize a small tactical hiring bar (2 infra hires) for 6 weeks to unblock provisioning and reliability work.

Town spotlight (all-hands) — narrative and run-of-show (12 min total exec segment + 18 min Q&A):
- Theme: "Serving at Scale — predictable, economical inference". Short arc: state where we are, what we will fix in next 90 days, how this impacts product and customers.
- Slides outline (for comms team): 1) State (1 slide): performance & business snapshot; 2) Focus (2 slides): the three priorities + quick KRs; 3) Impact (1 slide): customer stories & what success looks like; 4) Ask & how to help (1 slide): where volunteers/project pods can sign up.
- Live segment plan: CEO + CTO (6 minutes); Ops lead (Maya) (2 minutes) — announce owners; short demo/clip of a customer using Dedicated (2 minutes); open Q&A (18 minutes).

Risks / open questions (raw):
- Risk: pushing aggressive batching could regress quality for some prompts — need guardrail evals and a rollback policy.
- Risk: Dedicated provisioning automation depends on a third-party infra tool (contract negotiation open).
- Open question: what is the inverse relationship we accept between cost reductions and latency increase at the 95th percentile? Tradeoff guidance requested from CTO/SRE.

6-week experiment backlog (seed, pick top 3):
1) Intelligent batching pilot on 10% of traffic for the largest hosted customer (measure: token-cost delta, p95 latency). Owner: Priya. Jira: ENG-1056.
2) Dedicated fast-provision prototype using config templating + infra API (measure: time-to-provision). Owner: Jordan. Jira: ENG-1024.
3) Compliance pilot packaging for Private: create template runbook and legal artifact checklist for two prospects. Owner: Ethan. Jira: JIRA-4401.

Ownership & immediate actions (who does what in next 7 days):
- Priya Shah: refine batching experiment spec + pick 3 benchmark prompts (due 2025-03-12).
- Jordan Kim: prototype provisioning template (due 2025-03-14).
- Maya Rodriguez: finalize townline slides + speaker notes; schedule dry run with comms (due 2025-03-11).
- Liam O'Connor: coordinate with sales on Private pilot prospects, pull contract timelines (due 2025-03-12).

Logistics for weekend sync (workshop format):
- Friday afternoon async prep: read this doc, look at linked artifacts, add comments.
- Saturday 9:00–10:30: priority review & OKR seed (execs + leads).
- Saturday 11:00–12:30: experiment selection & rapid planning (cross-functional pods).
- Sunday 9:00–11:00: commit staffing + published brief + townline draft.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the townline simple — one big narrative only. Avoid 12 micro-asks.
- Find a 30s customer clip showing Dedicated uptime wins — ask CS for clips.
- We should have a very short rollback play for batching: toggle per-customer.

Links & artifacts (quick refs):
- Benchmark deck (internal): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Perf-Benchmarks-Q1
- Batching experiment epic: ENG-1056
- Provisioning prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/678
- Legal checklist draft (internal): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/LEGAL/Private-Checklist

Next steps / immediate asks for reviewers:
- Execs: confirm owners and the ask for two tactical hires by Mon EOD.
- Leads: comment inline on KRs and add missing metrics by Tue.
- Comms: draft 4-slide townline for CEO + CTO dry run by Wed.

Version notes: working draft v0.1 — will iterate during the weekend.

-- end of brief --

(informal edit log)

- 2025-03-07 Jordan: clarified provisioning KR and ETA
